title: Quarterly experiment slate: reservation strategy and autoscale orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run a focused quarterly program to validate two complementary strategies for reducing unit cost and improving resiliency for Dedicated pools: 1) reservation slicing + hedged burst windows (reserve smaller corridors and use burst reservoir for tails); 2) autoscale orchestration improvements that fast-fail cold starts and surface warm-pool suggestions. The intent is experimental: ship small hypotheses, measure unit cost and SLO change, and decide what to fold into our Q3 roadmap for Dedicated. This ticket coordinates PM, runtime, infra, and finance for the slate and consolidates results for the OKR review.
goals: Demonstrate >=8% reduction in per-token cost for steady-state traffic without regressing p95 latency beyond 5%
Validate hedged reservation window concept for predictable tail handling with <10% additional monthly cost for safety reservoir
Prove autoscale orchestration can reduce cold-start incidents by 60% for medium burst scenarios
Produce playbook with guardrails and rollout plan for production enablement
deliverables: Two canary pilots in us-west1 and eu-central1 for 4 weeks each
Dashboards: cost, latency p50/p95/p99, cold starts, queue depth
Playbook draft: rollout steps, abort criteria, billing guardrails
Final evaluation memo for OKR review with recommended next steps
milestones: 2026-03-31: Runtime canary implementation complete (kernel scheduling + prewarm triggers)
2026-04-07 to 2026-04-30: Canary observation window (2 regions staggered)
acceptance_criteria: All dashboards show telemetry for experiment cohorts and control cohorts
Cost model reconciled with Finance and sample billing reviewed
Abort conditions documented and automated rollback tested
Playbook includes migration path, API hooks, and console toggles for ops

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Experiments increase tail latency for non-canary customers. Mitigation: strict isolation in routing and traffic tagging, automatic rollback by agent
Risk: Cost overruns from reservoir mis-sizing. Mitigation: finance-approved throttle, emergency cap on reservoir spend
Risk: Telemetry gaps. Mitigation: require instrumentation sign-off before any pilot traffic is routed
